{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"8864d8f402afe21be313095dd56cbd18e1b7eac2ad1c62695b8b3f24a73156bc","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle setup confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: practice-test chapter map, mirror fine-tuning, seat limits, left versus right push-pull turns, hand-over-hand steps, backing, pulling away and stopping, and the older texting rule versus the hands-free law","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: practice-test chapter map, mirror fine-tuning, seat limits, left versus right push-pull turns, hand-over-hand steps, backing, pulling away and stopping, and the older texting rule versus the hands-free law
Confusable pairs and continuation facts for getting ready to drive; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
The Rules of the Road practice test spans four chapters (B-4, B-5, B-6 and B-8), while Traffic Signs and Signals maps to B-3 alone and Alcohol, Other Drugs and Driving to B-7. [A01]
Why it matters: group study map; confusable one topic across four chapters versus one chapter.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A02
Do not slide the seat so far forward, or pull the steering column out so far, that steering becomes awkward. [A02]
Why it matters: group seat setup; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A02
Your seat position should give a clear view through the windshield, both side windows and every mirror. [A02]
Why it matters: group seat setup; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A02
If leaning back a little still shows you more than a glimpse of your car's rear corners in the outside mirrors, turn those mirrors outward. [A02]
Why it matters: group mirrors; confusable seeing a sliver of your car versus seeing its corners.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
A car without remote mirror controls may need a helper to set the passenger-side mirror correctly. [A02]
Why it matters: group mirrors; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
Try new mirror settings while parked, for example along a street watching passing cars, before driving into traffic with them. [A02]
Why it matters: group mirrors; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
Failing to belt yourself or to secure passengers in a car seat or booster seat can bring a fine, and the passenger-protection chapter covers the full rules. [A03]
Why it matters: group belts; links the safety belt chapter.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A03
A manual transmission lets the driver use gears instead of brakes to help slow the car, and you should shift to a lower gear going down steep hills. [A03]
Why it matters: group transmissions; confusable manual downshift versus automatic low gears.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A03
Your elbows should bend slightly when your palm reaches the top of the wheel, and you should never sit with your arms locked straight. [A03]
Why it matters: group hand position; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A03
Your hand position will change briefly while you work the turn signal, headlight dimmer or wiper controls. [A03]
Why it matters: group hand position; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A03
An arm resting on the door or out the window gives you less control of the wheel and could be severed in a sideswipe. [A03]
Why it matters: group hand position; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A04
In a push-pull left turn the left hand pulls down to about 7 o'clock while the right pushes up to about 1 o'clock; a right turn mirrors this, with the right hand pulling to about 5 and the left pushing to about 11. [A04]
Why it matters: group steering; confusable left versus right push-pull clock positions.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A04
For a hand-over-hand right turn, reach forward to grip the rim at 1 o'clock palm down, pull to 5 o'clock, repeat with the other hand, and return to 9 and 3 before counter-steering out. [A04]
Why it matters: group steering; confusable hand-over-hand versus push-pull.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A04
While backing, keep to idle speed or gentle acceleration and keep looking to the rear until the car has fully stopped. [A04]
Why it matters: group backing; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A04
Before pulling forward, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal if leaving a curb, then move your foot to the accelerator and press gently. [A04]
Why it matters: group moving forward; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A04
For a smooth stop, check your mirrors, ease off the accelerator, move your foot to the brake and press with steady pressure rather than stomping. [A04]
Why it matters: group stopping; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A04
Once you become a competent driver, the safest habit is not letting your attention to driving slip. [A04]
Why it matters: group attention; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A05
To guard against carbon monoxide, have the exhaust checked regularly, listen for unusual roaring under the car and close the fresh-air vent in heavy traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A05
The older 2009 rule bans reading or sending written messages on a hand-held device while moving, with a fine of up to $50 plus up to $10 court costs, and exempts on-duty police, firefighters and emergency workers. [A05]
Why it matters: group phone laws; confusable texting-only rule versus the broader hands-free law.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A05
The hands-free law also forbids reaching for a device in a way that takes you out of your seated, belted position, and watching, recording or broadcasting video on it. [A05]
Why it matters: group phone laws; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A05
In a marked school zone the hands-free exception does not cover drivers under 18, for whom hand-held use is a delinquent act. [A05]
Why it matters: group phone laws; confusable adult school-zone rule versus under-eighteen rule.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]
